known_before_this_freeze: All on m3-protocol-1's spent pilot seeds 10900 to 10919 and nothing else. (a) Three scratch diagnoses, not ledgered and writing nothing to evals/ (their scripts were in the agent's scratch space, not the repository): the area ratio by the actual tool point's distance from the current cube (0.949 to 1.000 beyond 80 mm with the cube on the table, 9% of frames; 0.508 to 1.022 beyond 50 mm; 0.43 to 1.94 anywhere on the table); a commanded tool-point rule (more than 80 mm from the cube's initial centre, as a prefix), rejected because the arm starts 76 to 121 mm from the cube and 3 of 20 candidates had no checkable frame; and the sightline rule below. (b) The ledgered diagnostic that replaces them for the record: run 20261107T112025Z_3f2d4bd9 at clean commit 2bcc4f0 (src/vishwaroop/synth/size_rule_diagnostic.py), measured in simulation. For the commanded-joint sightline prefix at clearance 0.02 / 0.025 / 0.03 / 0.035 / 0.04 / 0.05 m: the fewest size-checkable frames 16 / 16 / 16 / 16 / 11 / 0 (the 16 from the two planning-failure episodes 10907 and 10916, T = 15, every frame checkable; among full-length episodes the fewest were 37 / 33 / 30 / 27 at 0.02 to 0.035 m, seed 10917); the share of frames 30.4% / 25.5% / 22.4% / 19.5% / 16.5% / 11.4%; the area ratio's minimum in them 0.957 / 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000 (maximum 1.000 throughout); the cube's largest displacement in them 1.6e-6 m throughout. At 0.035 m the median n was 33.5 and the smallest actual-joint clearance in a size-checkable frame 0.0353 m. Initial clearances ranged from 0.0437 to 0.1117 m. The area ratio's minimum over every frame was 0.176, so protocol-1's band kept as the presence band excludes a missing cube on these seeds. The 0.035 m clearance was chosen from (b): the smallest of the tested values with a 0.015 m margin above the first one where the ratio fell below 1. (c) The review before this freeze estimated, from a Monte Carlo over ManiSkill's cube-placement and rest-pose noise (not measured), that about 0.75% of scenes start with a clearance at or below 0.035 m (n = 0); hence n = 0 is not a failure and a short resize source is replaced. (d) Under protocol-2 frame injections of types 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 keep protocol-1's step draw, so most land after the size-checkable frames; types 1 and 2 are then caught by the presence band and extra_red, as in protocol-1. Nothing has been simulated on seeds 10200 to 10259, 10300 to 10319, 10400 to 10459, 10750 to 10759 or 10800 to 10899.

ET-M3-1.statement: Generation runs only from known sim scenes, with the initial state and asset hashes saved first; a scene-consistency check rejects injected mismatches.
ET-M3-1.candidate: a candidate is (i) a candidate manifest: the snapshot manifest's task id and version, seed, asset sha256s, cube half size and colour, and goal position; (ii) frames 0 to T of one recorded episode on that scene, rendered at 512 x 512 from the human render camera, frame 0 after restore_state and frame t after control step t; and (iii), for frame eligibility only, the joint positions and cube position that restore_state of the scene's saved initial state returns, the human render camera's centre (the translation column of the snapshot manifest's cam2world_gl), and the candidate's actions a_1 to a_T, a_t being the absolute pd_joint_pos target applied at control step t. An injection alters frames and the manifest, never (iii). No generator exists yet, so physics frames stand in for generated frames.
ET-M3-1.size_checkable_frames: The sightline is the segment from the camera's centre to the cube's initial centre. The arm's skeleton at a joint vector is arm_segments in the pinned src/vishwaroop/sim/so100_kinematics.py: line segments, without the links' thickness, from the base (world position (-0.725, 0, 0), yaw pi/2) through each joint origin of the mani_skill 3.0.1 SO-100 URDF chain in order to the fixed jaw's frame, then to the fixed jaw tip, and through the moving jaw's origin to its tip. Its clearance is the shortest distance from any skeleton segment to the sightline. Frame 0 is size-checkable when the clearance at the initial joint positions is more than 0.035 m; frame t >= 1 when frame t - 1 is and the clearance at a_t (all six values) is more than 0.035 m. So the size-checkable frames are frames 0 to n - 1, n between 0 and T + 1: the frames before the arm is first commanded near the sightline. The clearance is tested at the commanded targets only, not at the rendered arm, which lags them. Because the sightline ends at the cube's centre, a clearance above 0.035 m also keeps every skeleton segment more than 0.035 m from that centre. Both are geometric proxies; the pilot checks their premise in the simulator (stops 2 and 3). No image, mask or cube-area measurement enters this rule, so a resized, removed or duplicated cube cannot change which frames are size-checkable.
ET-M3-1.episode_kind: on even seeds the nominal scripted demo (VARIANTS['nominal']); on odd seeds an operator episode, m3-synth-lateral-miss and m3-synth-close-high alternating by seed, drawn as F2's rule in evals/M3-exit-tests.json
ET-M3-1.tolerance_pilot: block 10 seeds 10300 to 10319, used for nothing else, with the same nominal and operator alternation. The masks (red: R > 120, G < 60, B < 60; green: G > 120, R < 80, B < 80; 8-connectivity) and the rule are protocol-1's: each tolerance is the pilot's observed extreme widened by 10% (upper extremes x 1.1, lower x 0.9). The presence band [p_lo, p_hi] takes the area ratio's extremes over every frame, as protocol-1's band did, without limits. The size band [a_lo, a_hi] takes them over size-checkable frames only, subject to 0.36 < a_lo and a_hi < 2.56. The merge radius, first-frame tolerance, goal-centroid distance and minimum green count are taken over every frame, as before. The pilot records each candidate's n, and at every frame the simulator's cube position and the sightline clearance of the simulator's actual joint positions. It evaluates every condition below and, if any holds, writes nothing to evals/, lists all that hold, and the owner is told before any control or injection is generated: (1) more than 2 of the 20 pilot candidates have no size-checkable frame t with 1 <= t <= T - 1; (2) in a size-checkable pilot frame the simulator's cube centre is more than 0.005 m from its initial position; (3) a size-checkable pilot frame's area ratio is outside [0.95, 1.05], so the size is not knowable there; (4) the widened size band is not inside its limits; (5) a pilot frame shows no cube, so the presence band cannot exclude a missing cube; (6) no pilot frame is size-checkable; (7) a snapshot render shows no cube or no goal. A snapshot without an exposed render camera refuses the run, before any result is written. Otherwise the tolerances go to evals/M3-checker-tolerances.json with protocol_version m3-protocol-2 and sightline_clearance_m 0.035, and its sha256 is recorded in the status ledger before any control or injection is generated.
ET-M3-1.controls: 60 unmodified candidates on block 10 seeds 10400 to 10459
ET-M3-1.injections: 10 of each of six types, seed = 10200 + 10 x (t - 1) + i for type t = 1 to 6 and i = 0 to 9, each injected into its own unmodified source candidate on that seed, exactly as evals/M3-exit-tests.json's ET-M3-1 'injections' describes (so a source with T < 2 gives no injection of types 1, 2, 4, 5 or 6, which counts as not rejected; a type-3 source with T < 2 has an empty list below and is replaced), with these changes. rng = random.Random(seed); its first draw is the injection step: rng.randrange(1, T) for types 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6, and for type 3 (cube resized) rng.choice of the list of size-checkable frames t with 1 <= t <= T - 1, in ascending order. A type-3 source whose list is empty is replaced by the next unused seed from 10800 upward (to 10899) whose source's list is not empty, every skipped seed listed with its n and T; the replacement's rng is random.Random of the replacement seed, and its episode kind is the one it has within the single ascending sequence 10800 to 10899 under episode_kind's rule (so F2's lateral-miss count runs over that whole sequence). If 10800 to 10899 run out, that injection is not built and counts as not rejected. Every later draw follows in protocol-1's order. Type 6 replaces frame 0 by the snapshot render of seed + 500 (seeds 10750 to 10759), rendered for this purpose only.
ET-M3-1.checker: deterministic, with no learned part, every check applied to every candidate: manifest: the candidate manifest's fields equal the snapshot's; frame_shape: every frame has the render's shape; first_frame: frame 0 equals the snapshot's saved render within the first-frame tolerance; cube_area: in every frame, the red components within the merge radius of the largest one's centroid together have an area within [p_lo, p_hi] x the snapshot render's cube area; cube_size: in every size-checkable frame, that area is within [a_lo, a_hi] x the snapshot render's cube area; extra_red: in every frame, no other red component of at least 0.25 x that area exists; goal_centroid: in every frame with at least the pilot's minimum count of green pixels, the green goal pixels' centroid is within the goal-centroid distance of the snapshot's. A candidate with no size-checkable frame (n = 0) gets no cube_size check; every other check, cube_area in every frame included, still applies, and the candidate is reported as size not checked.
ET-M3-1.threshold: 100% of the 60 injected candidates rejected, an injection counting as rejected only when its unmodified source candidate passes every check and the injected one fails at least one (an injection whose source fails, or that is not built, counts as not rejected); and at most 3 of the 60 controls (5%) falsely rejected
ET-M3-1.if_it_fails: recorded as failed. A further revision needs m3-protocol-3, the owner's decision, a new tolerance pilot on block 10 seeds no protocol has used, and fresh controls and injections on new seeds
ET-M3-1.reported: rejections by type and by the check that caught each; every source candidate's own result; false rejections with their cause; the false-rejection count with its Wilson 95% interval; how often the size check runs: for every candidate (pilot, controls, sources) its n and frame count, and for the pilot, the controls and the sources the number of candidates with n = 0, the number with no size-checkable frame 1 to T - 1, the minimum, median and maximum n, and the share of all frames size-checked; each type-3 injection's seed, any skipped seeds, its step and T; the pilot's largest cube displacement and smallest actual-joint clearance in a size-checkable frame, and its size-checkable area-ratio range; what happens at n = 0 (above); the limits below; and a statement that controls are physics renders, so this does not estimate false rejection on generated frames (ET-M3-2 measures that)
ET-M3-1.limits: The size band runs only in the frames before the arm is first commanded near the sightline, typically the opening frames, so a size error that starts later is caught only if it leaves the every-frame presence band. Passing ET-M3-1 shows that the checker catches a resize that starts before the arm approaches, not that it judges cube size while the cube is grasped, carried or placed. ET-M3-2's freeze has to judge cube size in frames that were not size-checked.
